title: Why the Sky Is Blue
passage:
On a clear afternoon, the sky above us appears brilliantly blue, but sunlight itself is not blue at all. Sunlight is actually a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow, from red and orange to blue and violet. Each color travels as a wave with a different length, and while red light has relatively long waves, blue and violet light have considerably shorter waves.

When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with tiny molecules of gas, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. These molecules are far smaller than the wavelengths of light, and they scatter short waves much more strongly than long ones. As a result, blue light bounces in every direction across the sky, and wherever we look, some of that scattered blue light reaches our eyes. Scientists call this process Rayleigh scattering, after the British physicist who explained it in the nineteenth century.

Violet light is scattered even more than blue, so why is the sky not violet? There are two main reasons: the sun produces less violet light than blue light, and human eyes are considerably more sensitive to blue.

The same process explains why sunsets are often red and orange. In the evening, sunlight must travel through a much thicker layer of air before reaching us. Most of the blue light is scattered away along the journey, leaving the warmer colors to paint the horizon.

questions.stem: 'Waves' is a regular plural. Which of these words forms its plural in an IRREGULAR way?
options: wave
color
child
sunset
questions.why: Child→children is irregular; the others just add -s.

questions.stem: 'Violet light is scattered even more than blue, so why is the sky not violet?' What type of sentence is this?
options: A question
A command
An exclamation
A statement
questions.why: It asks something and ends with a question mark.

questions.stem: Why does blue light reach our eyes from every part of the sky?
options: The sun gives off only blue light
Gas molecules scatter it in all directions
Blue light has the longest waves
The sea reflects blue into the air
questions.why: Blue light 'bounces in every direction across the sky' after hitting gas molecules.

questions.stem: Which idea does the writer explain LAST?
options: What sunlight is made of
Who explained the scattering
Why the sky is not violet
Why sunsets are often red and orange
questions.why: The final paragraph explains red and orange sunsets.

questions.stem: How is red light different from blue light?
options: Red light has shorter waves and scatters more
Red light has longer waves and scatters less
Red light does not travel as a wave at all
Red light comes from the sun only at night
questions.why: Red light has long waves, and short waves are scattered much more strongly.

questions.stem: '…leaving the warmer colors to paint the horizon.' What is the effect of the word 'paint'?
options: It suggests people paint the sky
It says the horizon is made of paint
It makes the sunset sound like art
It shows that colors vanish at night
questions.why: 'Paint' is figurative: it compares the colorful sunset to a painting.

questions.stem: Which opinion is BEST supported by the passage?
options: Simple science can explain beauty in nature
The sky is blue because it reflects the sea
Scientists still cannot explain the blue sky
Sunsets are red because the sun gets cooler
questions.why: The writer uses scattering to explain both the blue sky and colorful sunsets.

questions.stem: Which information in the passage is LEAST complete?
options: What sunlight is made of
Which gases are most common in air
Why sunsets look red and orange
Why human eyes are more sensitive to blue
questions.why: The writer states this fact but gives no explanation for it.

options: A clear noon sky looks green all day long
The sky looks orange near the horizon at sunset
Sunlight reaches Earth as pure blue light
Red light scatters more strongly than violet
questions.why: The passage explains why sunsets are red and orange; the others contradict it.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST alternative title for the passage?
options: How to Paint a Sunset
The Life of a British Physicist
Scattered Light: Secret of the Sky
Why the Ocean Is Salty
questions.why: The passage explains how scattered light makes the sky blue.
